name: Hutaakan
traits: Tall, slender, jackal-headed humanoids with clawed feet. They generally go barefoot.

Adjust starting Strength down 1 and Wisdom up 1, keeping scores between 3 and 18. Any legal scores qualify. Wisdom is the prime requisite, with +5% XP at 13–15 and +10% at 16–18. Alignment is Neutral.

Advance in the Hutaakan class from 1st to 8th level, with one d4 per level. XP thresholds are 0, 1,200, 2,400, 4,800, 9,600, 20,000, 40,000 and 80,000. Use cleric saves of equal level. After the cap, each additional 400,000 XP earns a General Skill slot.

Base movement is 90′ per dungeon turn and 30′ per encounter round. Descending AC is 8 unarmored, 7 with either leather or a shield, or 6 with both. Cultural armor also includes scale, chain and banded mail. Ordinary shields are allowed, along with leather, scale or chain barding for riding lizards.
Cultural weapons are dagger, short sword, normal sword, mace, club, war hammer, throwing hammer, staff, whip, light and heavy crossbow, and sling.
Move silently and hide in shadows at thief percentages for the same level. Speak Hutaakan, Neathar, Orc and Gnoll. Take Honor Pflarr or Mysticism as a Wisdom-based General Skill.

With the additional apprenticeship XP, shaman casting can reach 8th level and wokan casting can reach 4th. Shamans may use cultural weapons except swords, plus all cultural armor. Wokani may use dagger, staff or sling and wear no armor.

name: Brute-Man
traits: Humanlike cave dwellers in laced hide clothing, generally hairier than neighboring humans, with a slightly receding forehead.

Starting Intelligence falls by 1 and Constitution rises by 1, bounded at 3 and 18. Strength and Constitution must each be at least 9. Strength is the prime requisite, with +5% XP at 13–15 and +10% at 16–18. Any alignment is allowed.

Advance in the Brute-Man class from 1st to 10th level with one d8 per level. XP thresholds are 0, 1,000, 2,000, 4,000, 8,000, 16,000, 32,000, 64,000, 130,000 and 260,000. Save as a cleric of the same level. After the cap, each additional 520,000 XP earns a General Skill slot.

Superior hearing prevents surprise by ambush. Gain +1 with individual initiative. On 1–3 on d6, detect hidden constructed features disguised as natural objects. Use the ordinary check for concealed features in other settings.
Leather is the cultural armor and shields are forbidden. Cultural weapons are hand axe, dagger, mace, club, blackjack, throwing hammer, staff, spear, javelin, short bow and sling.

Shaman and wokan apprenticeships go up to 4th spellcasting level apiece. Shamans may use hand axe, mace, club, blackjack, throwing hammer, staff and leather armor. Wokani may use dagger, club and staff and wear no armor.
Speak ka-na-to and Neathar. No General Skill is mandatory. Suggested skills include Fire-Building, mountain or hill Survival, Hiding and Danger Sense.

name: Kubitt
traits: An optional playable culture of humanlike people averaging 18 inches tall. Obtain DM approval for the option. Roll Strength on 2d6+1 and other scores on 3d6. Add 2 to Dexterity, capping it at 18.
Choose ordinary human cleric, fighter, magic-user or thief. With Dawn of the Emperors, forester and rake are available under that set’s rules. Use normal class advancement and Hit Dice.

Miniature armor and shields grant the same descending AC as full-sized equivalents. Cultural armor includes leather, scale, chain and banded mail and ordinary shields. Chain plus shield starts at AC 4. The miniature weapon table gives its own damage. Club, dagger and sling deal 1d2. Crossbow, hand axe, mace and short sword deal 1d3. Bow, spear, normal sword and war hammer deal 1d4. Battle axe, pole arm and two-handed sword deal 1d6.

Miniature short/medium/long weapon ranges are bow 10/30/50, crossbow 15/30/45, sling 10/20/30 and spear 5/10/20. Battle axe, bow, crossbow, pole arm and two-handed sword require two hands and lose initiative under the printed Kubitt rule.

A normal reach limit of 2 feet above the floor applies to manipulating or reaching things. A Kubitt pole arm allows strikes up to 4 feet above the ground. Movement matches a similarly encumbered human, with 6-foot bounds when running.
Move silently and hide in shadows as a thief of equal level. A Kubitt thief adds 10 percentage points to both abilities.

Typical gear is black armor and a black shield bearing a personal or family design. The four languages are Alphatian, Neathar, Nixie and Dryad. No General Skill is mandatory. Hiding, Riding a forest animal and Treewalking are common.

name: Schattenalfen
traits: Pale subterranean elves typically near 5 feet tall, with white or gray hair and blue or gray eyes. Dark, heavy clothing and broad-hooded cloaks protect them above ground.

With starting Intelligence 16–18, a Schattenalf may use the ordinary elf class. Others use the warrior-elf from Player’s Guide pp. 6–8. Both start with a d6 Hit Die. The warrior-elf has no initial spellcasting, levels up at 2,000 XP and reaches 10th at 360,000 XP on its own track.

A warrior-elf can learn magic in the outer world by investing XP in its separate casting track, advancing at most two caster levels per warrior level and never above its warrior level. The tracks can consolidate into the ordinary elf progression when their levels match. The boxed set also describes the catch-up option at 10th level.
Keep the elven infravision, detection and immunity to ghoul paralysis. This culture speaks Elvish, Neathar, Azcan, Traldar and Malpheggi.
Take 1 HP of damage for every hour with skin exposed to direct sun. Heavy, dark clothing that covers the whole body prevents it.

A broad cultural armory includes most infantry arms, bows, crossbows, sling and lances, along with all the usual body armors and ordinary shields. Flapsails have no barding. Choose Caving and at least one professional or labor General Skill.
